title_en: Psychology Made Simple (19/20): I'm Here with You
note_en: 与其A，不如B means "rather than A, better to B": 与其急着讲什么道理，不如先安静地陪着她 "rather than rushing to lecture her about anything, it's better to just sit quietly with her first." The two words come as a pair, 与其 before the rejected option and 不如 before the preferred one. English often reverses the order ("better to stay with her than to lecture"), but Chinese always puts the rejected choice first.
